[USER] User has 20 dozen fresh eggs from their coop.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant provided tips on how to store eggs properly, including:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] - Store eggs in a cool, dry place, ideally between 40°F (4°C) and 50°F (10°C).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] - Refrigerate eggs at a consistent temperature below 40°F (4°C).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] - Store eggs in their original carton or a covered container.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] - Store eggs with the pointed end down.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] - Avoid washing eggs before storing them.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] - Regularly check eggs for cracks or unusual odors.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] - Use the oldest eggs first (first-in, first-out).  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] - Label and date the carton with the collection date.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] - Avoid stacking eggs on top of each other.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] - Eggs can be frozen by beating them and storing in an airtight container.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Assistant mentioned that eggs can be stored for 4 to 5 weeks in the refrigerator and 1 year or longer in the freezer.
